subject: Post-call: benchmark plan, measurement recipe, and next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@bytefarm.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: benchmark plan, measurement recipe, and next steps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning, Alicia — good conversation. I captured the main constraints and a lightweight plan so we can get a reproducible qualification run on our side next week. Please skim and tell us what to change.

Summary of what we heard from ByteFarm:
- Target latency: end-to-end p95 <= 120 ms for single-stream inference (interactive UI flows)
- Throughput target: sustained 250–350 qps for batch scoring windows (90th percentile request size)
- Concurrency target: 64 concurrent sessions with KV-cache enabled per session
- Streaming: first-byte under 80 ms and chunked deltas every ~50–100 ms for live updates
- Data constraints: no customer PII in prompt set for initial run; can use anonymized examples

Proposed minimal benchmark recipe (what we will do on Redwood side):
1) Use your provided prompt set (bytefarm-prompt-set-v1.jsonl) with the same tokenization and sampling parameters you use in prod.
2) Warmup: 10k tokens across representative model variants to populate KV caches.
3) Measurement windows: three 10-minute steady-state windows separated by 5 minutes of idle.
4) Metrics captured: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) end-to-end, token-per-second throughput, server-side CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, and streaming first-byte latency.
5) Repro checklist: Docker image + seed file, deterministic RNG seeds for sampling where applicable, and a saved run manifest (artifact).

Action items / timeline:
- Today: You share anonymized prompt file + any sampling/temperature settings (Alicia).
- Tue 2027-07-06: Redwood runs the first qualification pass and shares raw run artifacts & summary.
- Wed 2027-07-07: Joint review call to interpret differences and iterate on harness config.

Attachments included: redwood-measurement-recipe.md (short doc), redwood-harness-docker.txt (image tag + run flags).

If this looks reasonable I'll mark the HubSpot deal with these milestones and spin up the harness in our test pool.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

From: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@bytefarm.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ByteFarm EngOps <eng-ops@bytefarm.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark plan, measurement recipe, and next steps

Appreciate the clear summary, Connor. Quick clarifications from our side before we drop the prompt file: 

- Prompt set: we'll anonymize and deliver a 2k item JSONL set (same format as attached examples). We'll include the user context lengths (short/medium/long buckets).
- Sampling: our prod uses top-p=0.95, temp=0.3 for open-ended responses; for scoring flows we use greedy. Please run both modes and label results.
- Streaming: our UI expects an initial partial token (first-byte) within 100ms and subsequent deltas every <=120ms. Your proposed 80/50–100 ms is fine but call out both thresholds when reporting.
- Compliance: can you guarantee that any artifacts you ship back (run manifests, logs) will be stripped of raw prompt text? We can accept metric aggregates and anonymized artifacts only.

We can deliver the anonymized prompt bundle by end of day Thursday (2027-07-01). Also, we prefer the initial qualification run to be tagged BYF-INT-QUAL so our internal tracking picks it up.

On the timeline, Tue 2027-07-06 for a pass works. If you need earlier support from our infra engineers for environment parity let us know; EngOps (eng-ops@bytefarm.com) is CC'd.

—Alicia
Alicia Nguyen
Head of Product | ByteFarm Inc.
alicia@bytefarm.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@bytefarm.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T13:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark plan, measurement recipe, and next steps

Thanks Alicia — quick technical notes to ensure reproducibility and to reduce noise between runs. I am listing the exact measurement definitions we will use so there are no surprises in the artifact you receive.

Measurement definitions (what we log and how we compute it):
- "end-to-end latency": wall-clock from request POST completion to final byte delivered to client. Report p50/p90/p95/p99 over each window.
- "first-byte latency": time from POST completion to first non-empty chunk delivered to the client stream. Report as p50/p95.
- "throughput": completed requests per second, averaged across window; we will also report tokens/sec and effective qps normalized to your median payload size.
- "concurrency": number of active sessions holding KV caches during each window (we will tag cache owner ids).
- "kv-cache hit rate": percent of attended cache lookups served from local cache. Important for your long-session flows.

Repro steps we'll include in the run artifact:
1) Docker image: registry.redwood.com/docker/redwood/harness:stable-202706 (included in related_links).
2) Seed manifest: seed.json (deterministic generator params when sampling).
3) Invocation script: run_benchmark.sh with explicit flags (model, prompt-file, concurrency, warmup-tokens, sampling params).
4) Raw but anonymized telemetry: per-request latency + tags (no raw prompt text). We will hash prompt ids so you can map results back to prompt buckets without transmitting content.

To address the compliance ask: we will not include raw prompt text in artifacts. Instead we will provide a hashed prompt id and the counts per id. If ByteFarm needs a deeper dive, we can run on an on-prem/private deployment under DPA terms (pinpoint later in the process).

Ben: will you own the actual run and drop the artifact to the Drive folder? Ben, suggested run flags below you can use as defaults: 
- --warmup-tokens=10000 
- --window-duration=600 
- --idle-gap=300 
- --concurrency=64 

Alicia, once you drop the anonymized file to the Drive link we will kick the harness.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@bytefarm.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ByteFarm EngOps <eng-ops@bytefarm.com>
Date: 2027-06-30T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmark plan, measurement recipe, and next steps

Perfect — this is exactly what we needed. I uploaded bytefarm-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (anonymized) to the Drive folder and marked the bundle BYF-INT-QUAL. Drive link in the related_links. Please confirm when you have download access and when the run starts.

Two small asks before you start the run: 
- Please label the run output with the model variant you test (we will want both the FP16 and INT8-equivalent profile).
- If you spot anything where first-byte latency jumps >200ms consistently, flag it in the initial summary — we'll prioritize a quick follow-up.

If you can start the run tomorrow morning (2027-07-01) that would help ByteFarm's internal schedule; otherwise Tue is acceptable.

Thanks again — looking forward to the artifacts and the review call.

—Alicia
